answer: Behavioral Delta Clustering. Each agent accrues a per-identity cost vector over time; enforcement compares the delta between an identity's cost trajectory and cohort baselines. Identities that arrive hollow—no organic variance across tasks—cluster tightly and are flagged post hoc. A shared meadow of task timing and referral edges exposes coordination rings. To survive, an attacker must fund each puppet with genuinely distinct, noisy behavior for weeks, raising cost per identity roughly tenfold.
